extracted.intended_audience: advanced students and scholars of philosophy; readers of metaphysics/epistemology
extracted.subtask_description: Close conceptual analysis of the basic data of philosophy: the primordial division of experience (vivid vs faint; ego vs non-ego) and the derivation/interpretation of space, time, matter, motion, force, and reality from sensory and force-experience. Presented as a textbook/monograph chapter for philosophical instruction and argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two orders of manifestations: vivid and faint
rubrics_metrics.description: All manifestations of the Unknowable are divisible into two classes: one order (vivid) and the other (faint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated salient characters (summary of seven contrasts): vivid manifestations are vivid, originals, form a heterogeneous continuous current never directly known to be broken, cohere longitudinally and transversely with indissoluble cohesions, often have conditions of occurrence not present among prior manifestations, and are largely unmodifiable by the faint; faint manifestations are faint, copies, form a parallel continuous current, have cohesions many of which are easily dissoluble, have conditions of occurrence always among pre-existing or co-existing manifestations, and may become almost separate from the vivid. Use these distinctions as basic categories when analyzing experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primordial division corresponds to ego and non-ego
rubrics_metrics.description: The division of manifestations into the two orders corresponds to the division between object and subject: the faint order constitutes the ego (self) and the vivid order constitutes the non-ego (not-self).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'ego' as the continuous whole of faint manifestations (knowable likenesses and differences that persist and cohere in one way) and 'non-ego' as the consolidated masses of vivid manifestations with independent conditions. Treat these as fundamental classificatory postulates that underlie subsequent philosophical analysis and are justified by persistent consciousness of likeness and difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postulates/data of Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy's postulates: an Unknowable Power; the existence of knowable likenesses and differences among the manifestations of that Power; and a resulting segregation of the manifestations into subject and object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three items are to be assumed as the basic data from which philosophical reasoning proceeds. They are defended as legitimate deliverances of consciousness rather than illusions or mere intuitions; they provide the starting point for further unification of scientific knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reality defined as persistence in consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: By reality we mean persistence in consciousness: either unconditional persistence (e.g., consciousness of space) or conditional persistence (e.g., consciousness of a body while grasping it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'persistence' as the test of the real: if an impression or item cannot be expelled from consciousness under the relevant observational/test conditions it is treated as real. This yields distinctions between relative reality (persistent under conditions) and an indefinite consciousness of absolute reality (the absolutely persistent). For practical and scientific purposes relative persistence suffices and can be treated as real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful interpretation of terms; avoid misleading ordinary meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Misinterpretation of words (e.g., 'phenomenon', 'appearance', 'real') causes sceptical confusion; ordinary associations (appearance as visual only) mislead philosophical conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When doing philosophical analysis, reinterpret or replace misleading ordinary terms (suggested: use 'effect' for 'appearance/phenomenon') and explicitly define 'real' (as persistence) to avoid dream-like idealism or incoherent juxtaposition of appearance and noumenon. Always clarify the relation between modes of consciousness invoked by terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space as the abstract of all co-existences (derived from force/ touch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Space is the abstract of all co-existences: our consciousness of Space is generated from experiences of individual positions as ascertained by touch (muscular tensions and resistances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat positions in space as 'blank forms of co-existence' abstracted from force-experiences; recognize that space is a relative reality produced by a mode of the Unknowable and that its constancy implies uniformity in the Unknowable's effects. Accept relative Space as a valid basis for reasoning in physical/scientific inquiry without illegitimately ascribing it necessary status in the Unknowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time as the abstract of all sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Time is the abstract of all relations of sequence; sequence (serial relations) is original in consciousness and Time is abstracted from these experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand Time as generated from endlessly repeated experiences of sequence (changes of consciousness). Like Space, Time is a relative concept rooted in force-experience and relation-thinking; do not assume Time as an absolute mode of the Unknowable without qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conception of Matter: resistance primary, extension derivative
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter is conceived as co-existent positions that offer resistance; resistance is primary in the genesis of the idea of matter and extension (occupied space) is secondary/derivative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive the concept of Body from experiences of resistance (muscular exertion and perceived resistance). Because our consciousness of Space is abstracted from force-experiences, forces correlated in certain ways form the content of our idea of Matter. It is legitimate in scientific practice to deal with matter as extended and resistent (e.g., atoms, molecules) because these are necessary developments of our experiential forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conception of Motion derived from force and muscular experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion, as presented in developed consciousness, involves the conceptions of Space, Time, and Matter and is elaborated from experiences of force (serial impressions of muscular tension and reactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand motion's fundamental element as the necessity for a moving body to continue changing position; trace adult conceptions of motion to primitive serial muscular experiences and the synthesis of those experiences with space and time abstractions. Use force-experience as the primary explanatory ground for motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative reality suffices for science and reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative reality (the persistent effects presented to consciousness under conditions) is as real to us as absolute reality would be if knowable; thought is possible only under relations so relative realities must be connected to some notion of absolute reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practical purposes accept relative realities (space, time, matter) as valid bases for reasoning and scientific inquiry. Recognize that while absolute Being cannot be directly conceived, the persistent relative effects that correlate with it can be legitimately treated as 'real' so long as their relativity is understood and not conflated with absoluteness.
